name: Fraumünster
overview: The Fraumünster is a historic church in Zurich famous for its stunning stained glass windows by Marc Chagall and Augusto Giacometti. This Gothic church has been a spiritual center of Zurich for over 1,000 years.
history: Founded in 853 AD by King Louis the German for his daughter Hildegard, the Fraumünster was once part of a powerful abbey that ruled Zurich until the 14th century. The current Gothic structure dates from the 13th-15th centuries.
highlights: Marc Chagall's famous blue stained glass windows (1970)
tips: Best viewed in morning when sunlight illuminates the Chagall windows. Small entrance fee for window viewing area. Photography allowed but no flash. Combine with Grossmünster visit across the river.
